clue.text: Perhaps New Zealander and South American will take hint by the first of October

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it inside, so the South American word wraps round the rest

parts.note: someone from the Andes mountain region of South America
a tip is a helpful hint

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word October is wanted here

parts.note: opening letter of the month

explanation.surface: A Kiwi and a South American pick up a hint as October begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks a New Zealander as one example; 'South American' looks like a second person in the scene but is really someone from the Andes.
explanation.definitionFit: New Zealanders and Australians live in the Antipodes, the lands on the opposite side of the globe from Britain.

clue.text: Excited to enter synagogue

indicators.note: the answer goes into the word that follows, sitting inside synagogue as a run of its letters

parts.note: the letters run consecutively in the middle of this word

explanation.surface: Someone is thrilled at the prospect of going into a synagogue.
explanation.definitionFit: To be all agog is to be eagerly expectant and full of excitement, a close synonym.

clue.text: Wood frames for the artwork

indicators.note: a frame is the border of a picture, so only the edge letters of each word are kept

parts.note: first and last letters of this short word
first and last letters of this word

explanation.surface: A carpenter makes wooden frames for some paintings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frames' looks like a noun about picture frames, but it is the instruction to take the outside letters of 'the' and 'artwork'.
explanation.definitionFit: Teak is a hard, durable timber from a tropical tree, an example of a type of wood.

clue.text: Lonely type, he recycled plastic

indicators.note: recycled material is broken down and remade, so these letters are reworked into a new order

parts.note: the twelve letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A solitary man reuses a piece of plastic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recycled' fits plastic perfectly in the surface, which hides its role as the rearrangement signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Polyethylene, also called polythene, is the commonest plastic, used for bags and packaging.

clue.text: Doctor and author has energy

parts.note: standard abbreviation for a doctor
the author speaking of themselves is I, and 'has' becomes the contraction 've

explanation.surface: A medic who is also a writer is full of vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: Crossword setters often call themselves the author, giving I; 'author has' is read as the contraction I've.
explanation.definitionFit: Drive means determination and vigour, the motivating force that makes someone work hard.

clue.text: Extra cover for Charlie's habit

indicators.note: to cover for something is to wrap round it, so the first word goes around the next

parts.note: something extra is an addition
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Cricket talk: an extra fielder at cover for a player named Charlie, who has a habit.
explanation.walkthrough: Extra cover is a cricket fielding position, which the surface leans on; the words are really ADDITION wrapped round C.
explanation.definitionFit: A habit in the sense of a dependency on a drug is an addiction, a compulsion hard to break.

clue.text: Finally cross bench and heave

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word cross

parts.note: the last letter of the word
a pew is a bench in a church

explanation.surface: Someone at last crosses a bench and strains to lift something.
explanation.definitionFit: To heave can mean to retch or vomit, so it matches spewing up the contents of the stomach.

clue.text: Each prison disturbed yet particular

indicators.note: something disturbed is thrown out of order, so the letters of the next word get rearranged

parts.note: as in so much per head, meaning each
nick is British slang for a prison or police station
the three letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Every jail inmate is upset, yet fussy about details.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang the nick is prison; 'disturbed' looks like it describes the prison but acts only on 'yet'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone pernickety is fussy and hard to please, the same as being particular about small details.

clue.text: Ladies curse their garments

parts.note: ladies are women
to curse is to swear

explanation.surface: Women complain angrily about their own clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Their' refers back to the ladies, so the definition depends on the opening word too.
explanation.definitionFit: Womenswear is the shop or trade term for clothing made for women, the ladies' own garments.

clue.text: Assorted mixture of island folk

indicators.note: a mixture blends things together, so the following letters are jumbled

parts.note: the ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A varied blend of people living on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Things of all kinds are of every variety, which is what an assorted selection contains.

clue.text: Designer uniform clothing could be a snare

indicators.note: clothing something means dressing it, so the designer label wraps around the next item

parts.note: Dr M, short for Dr Martens, the boot and shoe brand
Uniform is U in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A fashion house's uniform is a trap for the unwary.
explanation.walkthrough: Dr Martens is a British footwear brand; its name shortened to DR M goes around U. 'Could be' shows a snare is one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A snare is a type of drum with wires stretched across its lower skin, giving a rattling sound.

clue.text: Key justifier is one getting out of a bind

definitions.text: one getting out of a bind

parts.note: the escape key on a computer keyboard
an apologist argues in defence of something, justifying it

explanation.surface: Someone who makes excuses is the key to wriggling out of trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of a bind' sounds figurative, but the definition is literal: a performer freeing themselves from ropes and chains.
explanation.definitionFit: An escapologist is an entertainer who escapes from ropes, chains and locked boxes, like Houdini.

clue.text: Consequence concerning 10s

parts.note: re means about or concerning
the answer to 10 across in the plural: drums, a family of percussion instruments

explanation.surface: Something follows from the matter of a set of drums.
explanation.definitionFit: A repercussion is an unintended effect or result following an action, often an unwelcome one.

clue.text: Rise of criminal case circle in American region

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked, so the letters of the word case are twisted

parts.note: the four letters rearranged

indicators.note: in tells us the circle goes inside the region that follows

parts.note: Latin America, the Spanish and Portuguese speaking part of the Americas
a circle is shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A crime case grows out of a gang ring in an American district.
explanation.walkthrough: O goes inside LATIN to make LATION, which follows the rearranged case.
explanation.definitionFit: An escalation is an increase or intensification, so a rise in level or scale.

clue.text: Publication by creative artist beginning to exasperate judge

indicators.note: being creative means making something new, so the letters of artist are rearranged

parts.note: short for magazine
the six letters rearranged

indicators.note: the beginning of exasperate is its opening letter only

parts.note: the first letter of this word

explanation.surface: A magazine piece by an inventive artist starts to irritate a judge.
explanation.definitionFit: A magistrate is a civil officer who hears minor cases in a lower court, acting as a judge.

clue.text: Ghetto in Spain, both short of food

indicators.note: in places the first word inside the second
short means cut down, and both says each of the two words loses its last letter

parts.note: taken as written, then trimmed
taken as written, then trimmed

explanation.surface: A deprived quarter of a Spanish city is lacking in food.
explanation.walkthrough: Ghetto loses its O and Spain its N; GHETT then sits inside SPAI.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaghetti is a long thin pasta, a staple Italian food eaten with sauces.

clue.text: Around 55, losing cash yet computer literate

indicators.note: something losing its way goes astray, so the letters that follow are scattered
around says the rearranged letters wrap round the number

parts.note: the seven letters rearranged
5 is V in Roman numerals, written twice

explanation.surface: A pensioner of about fifty-five, going broke, can still handle a computer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Losing cash' looks like money trouble; 'losing' is the signal and 'cash yet' the letters. 55 is read digit by digit as V and V.
explanation.definitionFit: Tech-savvy describes someone well informed about and comfortable with modern technology, especially computers.

clue.text: Like gardens to be lopsided

parts.note: as means like
Kew Gardens, the Royal Botanic Gardens in London

explanation.surface: Some gardens are laid out unevenly.
explanation.walkthrough: Kew Gardens in west London is Britain's best-known botanic garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Askew means crooked or not straight, the same as lopsided or tilted to one side.

clue.text: Getting into taxi always pivotal

indicators.note: the answer gets into the following words, lying within them across the gap

parts.note: the letters run across the join of these two words

explanation.surface: Climbing into a cab is always crucial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pivotal' looks figurative, meaning crucial, but here it is literal: turning on a pivot or axis.
explanation.definitionFit: Axial means relating to or forming an axis, the line on which something pivots and turns.

clue.text: Syndicates regularly employed so-and- so to disrupt aortic treatment

indicators.note: disrupting something breaks it up, so the combined letters are thrown into a new order
giving something a treatment works it over, reinforcing that the letters are processed into a new order
regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter of the hyphenated phrase is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters
taken as written for the rearrangement

explanation.surface: Business groups regularly hire some fellow to upset a heart treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of so-and-so join aortic as the material to rearrange; the hyphens are skipped when counting.
explanation.definitionFit: Consortia, the plural of consortium, are associations of companies combined for a venture, just like syndicates.

clue.text: Not far from Mick Jagger's perhaps extraordinary worth

indicators.note: extraordinary means out of the ordinary, so the letters of worth are put out of their usual order

parts.note: Mick Jagger is a Rolling Stone; 'perhaps' marks him as one example of a Stone
the five letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Mick Jagger's fortune is remarkable, and not far off.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rolling Stones are the band Mick Jagger fronts, so he is a Stone and his possession is a Stone's.
explanation.definitionFit: A stone's throw is an idiom for a short distance, used of a place close by or nearby.

clue.text: Wading bird caught by another one

indicators.note: caught by means held inside the words that follow, so the answer lies within them

parts.note: the letters run across the join of these two words

explanation.surface: One wading bird is snatched by a second one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught' looks like the cricket abbreviation C, but here it means held inside the following words.
explanation.definitionFit: A heron is a long-legged, long-necked bird that stands in shallow water to catch fish.

clue.text: Pine for young woman

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to long for someone absent
second meaning: a title or term for an unmarried girl

explanation.surface: Someone longs for a young lady.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for feeling the lack of someone and also a noun for a girl or unmarried lady.

clue.text: Old impressionist briefly made a comeback

indicators.note: coming back means returning the way it came, so the letters are read in the opposite direction
briefly means cut short, so the painter's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Edgar Degas, the French Impressionist painter

explanation.surface: An elderly mimic briefly returned to the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Impressionist' suggests an entertainer doing voices; it is the painter Degas.
explanation.definitionFit: Aged means elderly, having lived a long time, a direct synonym for old.

clue.text: Country's intelligence captures central laboratory

indicators.note: to capture is to hold inside, so the intelligence measure surrounds the other letters

parts.note: intelligence quotient, a measure of intelligence

indicators.note: central points to the two middle letters of the ten-letter word

parts.note: the fifth and sixth of its ten letters

explanation.surface: A nation's spy service seizes a lab at its heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intelligence' suggests spies, but it is the IQ score.
explanation.definitionFit: Iraq is a Middle Eastern nation with Baghdad as its capital, so it is a country.

clue.text: Most important and complete part of Yorkshire

parts.note: something over is finished or complete
Yorkshire was historically split into three Ridings, North, East and West

explanation.surface: A key and whole area of a northern English county.
explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshire is a large county in northern England whose old divisions were called Ridings.
explanation.definitionFit: An overriding concern is one that takes priority over all others, so it is the most important.

clue.text: Want to be heard, do some baking!

indicators.note: being heard means we go by how the phrase about baking is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: to knead dough is part of baking bread

explanation.surface: Someone longs to be noticed while doing a spot of baking.
explanation.definitionFit: Need and want both mean to require or lack something, as nouns or verbs.

clue.text: It's no problem coming in puffed up and under the influence

indicators.note: coming in means entering, so the rearranged letters go inside the word for puffed up
a problem knocks things out of order, so the letters that came before are rearranged

parts.note: the five letters rearranged
hyped means exaggerated or promoted, puffed up

explanation.surface: Someone says it is no trouble as they arrive bloated and drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under the influence' usually means drunk; here it means in a trance.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone hypnotised is in a trance and under another person's control, swayed by their suggestions.
